hook.text: A maze is easier if you start from the exit. Working backward simplifies what forward thinking can't.

buildup.text: Backward reasoning starts from the desired goal and traces back to the current state, step by step.

discovery.text: It works best when the goal is clear but the starting moves are ambiguous—many paths forward, few backward.

twist.text: Mathematicians use it constantly. To prove X, assume X is true and see what must also hold.

climax.text: In planning, working backward from a deadline forces realistic scheduling that forward plans often miss.

punchline.text: Know where you're going. Then trace the path back.

quiz.question: When is working backward most useful?
options: When the goal is clear but starting moves are ambiguous
When the start is clear and the goal is vague
